title: shadowed-retries-silently-skip-meter-incrementing-on-enforcement-shortcircuit
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: We observed that a subset of routed fallback/retry requests were not producing meter increments and therefore were not counted by downstream billing aggregation. This manifests as quota enforcement gaps (customers appearing under their quota while actually sending tokens) and underreported usage in analytics dashboards. The bug sits in the enforcement short-circuit path inside the rate-policy engine: when a request is routed to a fallback model or route and hits the 'fast-allow' branch (path that skips some enforcement steps for latency), the meter emission call is skipped for shadow/retry flows that include the 'X-Shadow-Request' header. This results in missing ledger entries and incorrect per-key accounting.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a normal request to route /v1/generate with header X-API-Key=<org-key> and X-Trace-Id=trace-1; observe meter increment in /internal/metrics (token_count emitted).
2) Trigger path that causes fallback: configure a canary rule to reject primary model and route to fallback by setting header X-Force-Fallback: true.
3) Send the same request but include X-Shadow-Request: true to simulate shadowed retry; observe no meter increment for the fallback invocation in metrics and billing-aggregator logs.
4) Compare billing-aggregator ingestion: primary path emits events, but fallback/shadow path has no corresponding METER event and is absent from daily batch sums.
observed_behavior: Fallback/shadowed requests that take the enforcement short-circuit path do not create meter events; downstream billing aggregator and quota windows show lower usage than actual. Quota checks that rely on aggregated counts allow additional traffic beyond intended limits for impacted orgs during the window.
expected_behavior: Every request that consumes model tokens (including retries, shadowed duplicates, and fallback model invocations) must emit a canonical meter event with a stable request identifier so the billing aggregator can attribute usage exactly once per logical consumption. Short-circuit/fast-paths must not bypass meter emission.
impact_details: Affected customers: subset of orgs using routed fallbacks and internal replay/chaos tooling during 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC -> 2026-03-10 23:00 UTC. Estimated undercount: ~27k token units across 6 orgs (sampled estimate) and at least 3 quota bypass incidents where per-org enforcement did not block a burst. Business risk: incorrect billing and potential revenue variance, incorrect SLA/usage alerts, and customer trust damage.
root_cause: The enforcement pipeline contains an optimization: a "fast-allow" branch that performs minimal checks and returns early for latency-sensitive fallback routing. That branch assumed meter emission occurred earlier in the pipeline, but for shadowed/retry flows the normal pre-enforcement path is bypassed and the meter increment hook is not executed. Additionally, deduplication logic in the billing adapter treated shadowed requests with different shadow IDs as duplicates and silently dropped unmatched increments, which compounded the undercount.
mitigation: Hotfix: 1) Ensure meter increment is executed atomically before any short-circuit return, regardless of path (PR submitted). 2) Adjust billing-adapter deduplication to use a canonical logical id (X-Canonical-Request-Id) propagated from the ingress to fallback invocations. 3) Backfill estimates: run reconciliation job that scans request logs and synthesizes missing meter events for the affected window, injecting them into billing-aggregator with 'backfill' tag.
tasks: Create hotfix branch and PR that moves meter emission into the enforced critical section (ENG-214579-hotfix) - assigned to Liam Patel
Add instrumentation to enforcement code: counters for 'short-circuit-without-meter' and unit tests covering shadowed retry paths
Run canary deploy to oncall org subset for 2 hours and monitor billing-aggregator ingestion and per-route token delta
Implement reconciliation job prototype to synthesize missing meter events for 2026-03-09 -> 2026-03-10 window
Notify finance and CS with initial impact estimate and planned backfill schedule
Postmortem draft: collect traces, dashboard graphs, and timeline for incident report
attachments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/8142 (PR: hotfix - ensure meter emission before short-circuit)
rollback_plan: If the hotfix causes regressions in latency-sensitive paths, revert and deploy a guard: re-enable previous behavior and instead add an explicit meter emission stage earlier in the ingress pipeline with feature flag 'meter-critical-path=true' to progressively enable across regions.
